simple.meaning: אַדְרַזְדָּא (ʼadrazdâʼ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “quickly or carefully.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 7:23. The surrounding context includes family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַדְרַזְדָּא (H149) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H149. adrazda אַדְרַזְדָּא adverb correctly, exactly (according to Haug JBW 1853, 152 f. Scheft 68f. from Zend derez , make firm , whence Sanskrit participle passive drdha , firm, sure, suitable , Zend dere´ta , holding firm , Persian durust , whole, complete, correct ; > Nö KAT 2 617 from אַזְדָּא , q. v.); — Ezra 7:23 א ׳יִתְעֲבֵד . אֶדְרַע see דרע . אוה (√ of following; see Biblical Hebrew אוֺת , אוה ).

occurrences.englishText: Whatever is commanded by the God of heaven, let it be done exactly for the house of the God of heaven; for why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons?
